programme: STAT2-driven induction of PML (STAT2 targets PML directly), feeding a PML-organized p53/Rb-CDKN2A checkpoint (PML and KAT5 both converge on TP53/CDKN1A; ZBTB7A represses the same node via MDM2, CDKN2A, RB1, E2F4) that sits alongside an NF-kB inflammatory arm (RELA driving TNF, IL6, CXCL8, ICAM1, VCAM1, BIRC3), with ZBTB7A itself listed as a direct transcriptional target of... rather regulator of RELA in the given target sets, coupling the checkpoint arm to the inflammatory arm.
role_in_a: In COVID-19 this module is the interferon-to-restriction-factor axis: STAT2 signaling induces PML (an interferon-stimulated antiviral nuclear-body protein, consistent with STAT2's 0.98 Open Targets percentile), RELA runs the NF-kB cytokine output implicated in cytokine-storm inflammation (support: PMID 42063563 on RelA-driven lung epithelial antimicrobial response, PMID 40872607 on RelA in a COVID mechanism study), ZBTB7A is reported to promote virus-host homeostasis during coronavirus infection (PMID 36243002), and KAT5 repression tracks with oxidative stress/senescence in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells (PMID 34571838) — i.e. the checkpoint arm is being pulled toward senescence/restriction while RELA drives inflammation.
role_in_b: In head and neck cancer the same checkpoint arm (PML/CDKN2A/RB1/TP53, restrained by ZBTB7A and co-activated by KAT5) is the classic tumor-suppressor circuit disabled in HPV-driven HNC (E6 degrades p53, E7 inactivates Rb and drives compensatory CDKN2A/p16 loss); this matches PML's notably high Open Targets association with head and neck cancer (0.83 percentile, the strongest disease link of any factor in this list) and KAT5's identification as a candidate gene in an HPV-associated HNC target screen (PMID 36245368). RELA's role as an NF-kB driver of the inflammatory, invasive tumor microenvironment is the textbook HNC story, though the Open Targets score for RELA in this record is low (0.089), so this arm is asserted from general biology rather than from this record's HNC evidence.
shared_axis: Both diseases repeatedly force the same choice on epithelial cells under stress: whether an NF-kB-driven inflammatory response (RELA) resolves through a PML-organized p53/Rb-CDKN2A checkpoint (PML, ZBTB7A, KAT5) into senescence/clearance or is instead sustained/bypassed. In COVID-19 that checkpoint governs clearance versus persistence of infected airway epithelium; in HPV-driven HNC the same checkpoint is chronically disabled to permit immortalized growth, so the identical transcriptional module recurs despite the two diseases sharing neither tissue nor cause.
reasoning: The module is nameable directly from the given target-gene overlaps (STAT2→PML, ZBTB7A/PML/KAT5 all converging on TP53/CDKN1A/CDKN2A/RB1, RELA carrying the NF-kB output), and each arm has independent placement in at least one disease (RELA, ZBTB7A, KAT5 in COVID-19 via retrieved papers; PML and KAT5 in HNC via Open Targets score and one HPV-screen paper respectively). But no retrieved item states a COVID-19/HNC connection — the pairing is assembled by reasoning across separately documented roles, and STAT2 and PML themselves carry no on-topic paper, so support stops short of strong.
support: PMID 42063563 — RelA(RELA)-driven DNA binding supports lung epithelial antimicrobial response in a COVID-19 context; PMID 40872607 — RELA implicated in a network-pharmacology mechanism study of COVID-19; PMID 36243002 — ZBTB7A promotes virus-host homeostasis during human coronavirus 229E infection; PMID 34571838 — KAT5 repression linked to oxidative stress/senescence in SARS-CoV-2-infected neuronal cells; PMID 36245368 — KAT5 identified among candidate genes in an in-silico screen of HPV-associated head and neck cancer targets.
how_to_falsify: In SARS-CoV-2-infected airway epithelial cultures and in an HPV+ HNC cell line side by side, perturb ZBTB7A (knockdown/overexpression) and check by ChIP or CUT&RUN whether it binds the RELA promoter and the CDKN2A/RB1/MDM2 loci in both systems, and whether STAT2 binds the PML promoter after IFN/infection; if these binding events and the predicted downstream moves (RELA target induction up when ZBTB7A is lost, CDKN2A/RB1 checkpoint output down) do not occur concordantly in both cell types, the shared-module claim fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood versus head-and-neck, so any shared axis is a signaling module, not a shared cell type or anatomical link. The 184 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the denominator overstates independent confirmation. STAT1 and KLF9 were excluded as tissue-generic despite also being single-group leaders — correctly keeping this account off the canonical, tissue-agnostic IFN master regulator and resting instead on the paralog-specific STAT2 signal. Single-view exclusions (ZBTB33, ZBTB7B, LHX3, DLX3, ZHX2, CNOT7) confirm the story isn't built on one subgroup. CREB3, TCFL5, RARG, PEG3, HEY1, VENTX, and POU2F3 were deliberately left out of the programme: most have no Open Targets association and no on-topic paper for either disease, and their retrieved papers (AML fusion for RARG, Notch biology for HEY1, a generic secretory-pathway review for CREB3) are off-topic — including them would manufacture a broader story than the record supports.
